name: Emily Thornberry
role: British MP for Islington South and Finsbury (since 2005); former shadow foreign secretary
summary: Thornberry advocates public services, redistribution and government-led climate investment, alongside legal protection for abortion and transgender people. Her foreign-policy statements emphasize multilateral institutions, international criminal accountability and conditional support for humanitarian intervention.

universal-healthcare.rationale: She calls for proper investment in the NHS so people can access treatment, supporting the state-funded health service.

public-ownership.rationale: She endorses a publicly owned energy company investing in renewables, establishing support for a public role in energy ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: She explicitly proposed increasing tax rates on the wealthiest during her leadership campaign.

unions-good.rationale: Her Colombia speech praises unions’ struggle for justice and insists on protecting workers and their representatives.

property-fundamental.rationale: She proposes local-authority takeover of hoarded, unused land for housing, permitting public need to override owners’ control.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Her annual report endorses changing the law to make corporate fraud easier to prosecute.

cut-welfare.rationale: She calls for a welfare safety net without gaps through which whole families can fall.

decide-locally.rationale: At the reform hustings she supports giving communities meaningful control rather than merely responsibility for centrally imposed cuts.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: She voted for the Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Bill at second reading in February 2013.

abortion-legal.rationale: She supports abortion decriminalisation and implementation of abortion rights in Northern Ireland, opposing any rollback in Britain.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: She explicitly calls for strengthening the United Nations and working through multilateral institutions.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: She defends the Kosovo intervention and says military action can protect populations facing slaughter, subject to credible planning.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: She calls climate change an emergency requiring an urgent government-led transition to net zero and major green investment.

state-directs-investment.rationale: She endorses large public investment in green industries and publicly financed renewable generation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Asked about development partnerships, she describes herself as pragmatic and says policy should follow what works for actual needs.

force-without-un.rationale: She questions an absolute Security Council veto requirement and defends Kosovo intervention, while insisting on wider international legitimacy.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: She explicitly opposes new North Sea oil and gas licenses and mandatory annual licensing rounds.

proportional-representation.rationale: She supported proportional internal party elections but expressed reservations about changing Westminster’s constituency-based electoral system.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Her Colombia speech criticises impunity for human-rights abuses under Uribe and demands accountability through international pressure.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Her June 2021 report advocates returning British foreign-aid spending to 0.7% of national income.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Her later interview defends Britain having its own deterrent, although she declines to specify when it should be used.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: She demands enforceable worker protections in trade deals and opposes agreements undermining food standards or increasing carbon offshoring.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: She condemns mulesing of lambs as horrific and challenges importing meat linked to the practice.

animal-use-humane.rationale: She defends food and farming standards while challenging cruel treatment of livestock, accepting farming subject to welfare protections.

non-intervention.rationale: She rejects an absolute ban on intervention and supports responsibility to protect, with legal legitimacy and long-term planning.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Her report criticises unreported departmental spending and argues that MPs must obtain and reveal government information.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: She unequivocally supports gender self-identification and legal recognition, and calls for protection of transgender people.

assisted-dying.rationale: Her June 2025 explanation supports assisted dying for terminally ill adults and judges the bill’s anti-coercion safeguards adequate.

open-government-data.rationale: She praises departments publishing spending details up front and calls for government transparency to become standard.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Her defense of retaining Britain’s Trident deterrent is incompatible with excluding its nuclear weapons from British territory.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Her support for military intervention to protect civilians permits force beyond repelling an attack on Britain.

free-public-college.rationale: She pledged tuition-fee abolition in 2020 but defended retreat from that pledge in 2023 on economic grounds while retaining the aspiration.

public-service-media.rationale: She advocates a publicly funded BBC that is independent of government and trusted as a source of news.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: In 2019 she defended maintaining a nuclear deterrent with ambiguity about use, despite her earlier opposition to renewal.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Her report endorses International Criminal Court work to prosecute Putin and other leaders for crimes in Ukraine.

notes: Reviewed the entire 490-statement bank against evidence spanning her early parliamentary career, leadership campaign and later statements. No position is assigned from Labour membership alone. Her 2014 flag-photo controversy and apology do not establish a general view on national culture. On Trident, the later interview defending deterrence takes precedence over her earlier opposition to renewal; the record does not specify a willingness to launch a nuclear strike. On tuition fees, the low-confidence answer records both her earlier abolition pledge and later defense of abandoning it under changed economic conditions. General human-rights statements are not extended to specific unaddressed religious or criminal laws. No inference from absence, office-holding or party label is used.
